Changed chirplet calibration from a single repeated motif to a stateless timeline fingerprint. MimirChirpletCalibrationPhrase.ForIndex(N) deterministically generates phrase N; runtime emits N mod 16 every 3.25 seconds, and the analyzer searches the 16-phrase cycle. Each phrase is a birdsong-like asymmetric motif with six chirplets spread over about 1.38 seconds. Mimir.slnx built cleanly. A short BufferSmoke run completed without analyzer errors, but loopback emitted zero packets during that smoke, so it verified plumbing only, not fresh delay estimates.

Treat this as online emission/capture proven, online acoustic lock not yet solved.

Replaced the discrete 16-phrase chirplet cycle with MimirChirpletTimeline, a deterministic unbounded chirplet stream. MimirRuntime now continuously queues uncached 0.5-second PCM segments through Aquarium audio with 1 second of lead, and MimirAudioSynchronizationAnalyzer extracts continuous chirplet atom energy traces from loopback and mic windows rather than searching a finite phrase cycle. Short headless Mimir.App telemetry runs proved the actual runtime path now locks online: loopback and all six audio buffers were live, reports were produced, and sync states appeared for Focusrite, Kiyo, Kiyo Pro, and both PS3 Eye mics. Delay estimates are still jumpy enough that the fractional-delay/SRO actuator should wait for better state filtering.

Changed MimirChirpletTimeline from anonymous deterministic texture to an explicit order-3 de Bruijn symbol timeline over 32 separated chirp symbols. Any three consecutive correctly detected symbols identify a timeline event within the current operating horizon; reports now expose timelineMatchedEvents and timelineConfidence when event-index refinement is used. A synthetic check rendered two seconds of canonical timeline audio and decoded events 0, 1, and 2 back to a window start of -0.0015 seconds. Real headless app sniff did not provide a clean physical proof because Scarlett loopback capture again stopped advancing early; build remains clean.

Reworked MimirChirpletTimeline symbols from fixed frequency slots into time/frequency constellations. The order-3 de Bruijn sequence still gives three-chirp timeline placement, but each symbol now carries identity through start band, glide shape, duration, and following inter-chirp gap. Event start times are precomputed over the de Bruijn period instead of using a fixed stride. Synthetic verification rendered two seconds of canonical timeline audio and decoded interior events 9, 10, and 11 back to a zero-second window start, proving placement does not rely on the opening triplet.

Documented the intended decoder as a constrained chirplet transform: known dictionary projection to symbol observations, code-valid de Bruijn triplets to canonical timeline anchors, anchors to affine source clock fits, and delay/SRO from comparing loopback and mic clock fits. Added MimirChirpletStreamDecode records and MimirChirpletStreamDecoder with a bounded PCM window, absolute sample offsets, triplet anchors, and clock fits. MimirAudioSynchronizationAnalyzer now prefers matched decoded timeline anchors before falling back to the older chirplet-energy lag search. Synthetic self-test over two seconds of emitted timeline audio currently decodes 12 symbols and one correct anchor for event 9 at sample 47520 with clock 48000 Hz; this proves the new spine but also proves the symbol likelihood/codebook layer is not finished enough to place every triplet yet.

Replaced one-best-symbol triplet placement with a constrained transform/trellis pass. DecodeStreamWindow now emits transform frames with multiple symbol candidates per chirp, enumerates candidate triplets through the de Bruijn map, scores measured inter-chirp gaps, and keeps the coherent local clock path rather than accepting any random valid triplet. Synthetic two-second emitted timeline check improved from one anchor to 11 coherent anchors, including events 0-9, with fitted clock 47978.350 Hz, confidence 0.885, and 8.741 sample MAE. This is the right decoder shape; remaining work is symbol/codebook separation and sub-frame timing precision so the fit lands exactly at 48000 Hz and covers every emitted triplet.

Removed the legacy synchronization pipelines from live code. Separated chirplet symbol ownership into MimirChirpletSymbolCodebook and added per-candidate refined sample offsets to transform frames. The codebook now guarantees each of the 32 symbols has a unique chirp shape; rhythm is additional code evidence rather than an acoustic alias. Synthetic two-second emitted timeline check now detects all 15 emitted chirps, decodes 13 possible triplet anchors for events 0-12, and fits clock=48001.819 Hz with confidence=0.952 and MAE=5.171 samples, improved from 11 anchors / 47978.350 Hz / MAE=8.741.

Resource-backed Fensalir lowering now reaches planned packets but not visible rendering. Mimir audio spectrum/waveform surface intents use the source observation's mimir:resource:* key, so --fensalir-field-evidence-smoke produces one planned TubeField packet and two deferred non-backend claims. Fensalir's AquariumFieldScriptCompiler.CompileEvidence can bind declared resources in DSL; --fensalir-field-dsl-resource-smoke produces one planned TubeField packet with no deferred requests. The next blocker is engine-side D3D12 packet/resource resolution: Fensalir must import/alias GPU-resident structured buffers, textures, meshes, surface pages, and volumes and bind them to selected shader lowerings before planned packets can render visibly.

Corrected the resource-boundary model: Mimir is a client running inside the Fensalir runtime, so Mimir-declared buffers are Fensalir resource declarations, not cross-process payload truth. Fensalir now has the first D3D12 field resource registry cut for declared structured/curve buffers: valid declarations allocate/reuse/retire engine-owned GPU slots under the resource key, and duplicate resource keys are validation errors. Visible rendering is now blocked on TubeField shader binding for resolved slots, not on deciding who owns the buffers. Texture, mesh, surface-page, and volume resource kinds remain future Fensalir resolver cuts.

Tightened the resource invariant: rendering buffers should move to GPU residency ASAP and stay there, with Fensalir passing handles/SRVs/UAVs between compute and render lowerings instead of copying samples through CPU. Fensalir's TubeField DSL now describes 2D rolling Float32 buffers as Catmull-Rom XY tubes with modulo column addressing, amplitude power/normalization, radius scaling, ramp texture path, and emission scale. D3D12 shared structured/curve resources import by GPU handle or stay unsupported; Fensalir only allocates a GPU slot when it is the producer. Visible rendering still needs shader-side TubeField expansion/binding over the GPU slot.

Fensalir now has the first D3D12 TubeField rendering path for Mimir-declared rolling float buffers: compute shader expansion binds the resolved GPU sample buffer read-only, emits endpoint-clamped Catmull-Rom tube envelopes into fixed-budget vertex/index UAVs, honors declared sample stride with byte-address loads, draws opaque field geometry through the spline SDF pipeline, and reports requested/dispatched/truncated segment counts. Mimir build and both Fensalir field evidence smokes pass; remaining cuts are per-pixel source-row material sampling, ramp texture binding/fallback, indirect draw packets, and non-buffer resolvers.

Fensalir TubeField rendering now includes the pixel-material side Mimir asked for: compute expansion records one draw batch per lowering, and the TubeField pixel shader binds the matching source buffer/constants and resamples the rolling buffer per pixel by column+spline coordinate using the cheap 5-tap path. Initial material is opaque field geometry with fallback black-to-warm ramp, squared normalized emission, and fake Fresnel center-bright/edge-dark shaping. Real blackbody ramp texture binding, indirect draw packets, and non-buffer resolvers remain future cuts. Headless Fensalir dev reload, Aquarium.Engine.Tests, Mimir build, and both field smokes passed.

Fensalir now exposes Texture2D local asset resources for engine users. The field DSL accepts `texture2d id=... key=... path=...`, TubeField `ramp=...` resolves aliases to resource keys, D3D12 lazily uploads local Rgba8 assets and binds the ramp SRV with linear clamp sampling, and unresolved ramps use a Fensalir-owned 0-1 fallback texture. Mimir's DSL smoke now proves two resources, one TubeField lowering, automatic ramp handle binding, and one planned TubeField packet. Headless Fensalir reload, Aquarium.Engine.Tests, Mimir build, and both field smokes passed.

Fensalir TubeField compute now emits GPU-resident D3D12 indirect draw argument packets. Render still binds one batch at a time because source/ramp material root bindings differ, but draw count/start index authority now comes from the compute-emitted packet and render uses ExecuteIndirect. Fensalir build/tests/headless reload, Mimir build, and both field smokes passed. Remaining renderer migration cuts are mesh, surface-page, and volume resource resolvers.

Fensalir now resolves SurfacePage field resources. Contracts and DSL can declare GPU-resident 2D surface pages with dimensions, format, version, and optional local source; D3D12FieldResourceRegistry allocates empty shader-readable page textures or lazily loads local source-backed pages. This creates resource authority for future Height/SDF/material lowerings, but does not yet make a surface-page render lowering. Fensalir build/tests/headless reload, Mimir build, and both field smokes passed.

Fensalir now resolves VolumeTexture field resources. Contracts and DSL can declare GPU-resident 3D textures with width/height/depth/format/version, and D3D12FieldResourceRegistry allocates shader-readable Texture3D resources for future density/extinction/SDF3D lowerings. This is resource authority only, not a volume render lowering. Fensalir build/tests/headless reload, Mimir build, and both field smokes passed. Mesh remains the resolver that needs a real vertex/index ownership contract.

Fensalir now resolves Mesh field resources as one package: Mesh.Vertices and Mesh.Indices describe the GPU vertex/index buffers, with topology, index format, bounds, submesh count, and version on the package. The DSL accepts `mesh id=... key=... vertices=... vertexStride=... indices=... indexFormat=... topology=...`, and D3D12FieldResourceRegistry allocates/reuses the GPU-resident buffers under the mesh resource key. This is resolver authority only; mesh draw/material lowerings remain future work. Fensalir build/tests/headless reload passed.

Fensalir's evidence DSL can now plan generic resource-backed claims with `claim id=... resource=... encoding=... layer=...`, so Mesh, SurfacePage, and VolumeTexture resources reach backend packet planning. The remaining renderer cut is blocked on selected render-lowering contracts: Mesh drawing needs explicit vertex attribute/material semantics because count/stride/index format only describe buffer shape, not how bytes become position, normal, uv, color, transform, or material.

Clarified Fensalir Mesh layout authority: imported/user-facing FBX/OBJ-style meshes use the standard PositionNormalUvColor vertex layout, while generated meshes declare PipelinePrivate and let their selected lowering own the exact minimal byte layout. The generic mesh ABI is no longer the blocker; next renderer work should choose the first selected mesh/page/volume lowering and material path.

Fensalir TubeField now renders through the first explicit pipeline-private generated mesh lane. Compute owns the private D3D12TubeFieldVertex/index/indirect argument layout; render binds those buffers as a D3D12PipelinePrivateGeneratedMesh before applying TubeField source/ramp/material root bindings and ExecuteIndirect. This follows the generated-mesh option without adding a public imported mesh renderer.

Fensalir lifted the DrawIndexed indirect command signature from TubeField to the generated-mesh lane. TubeField still emits its own indirect argument buffer, but future pipeline-private generated mesh lowerings can share the same five-uint D3D12 DrawIndexedArguments ABI with their own producer buffers/material bindings.
